hero.heading: Ask your homelab what's going on.
hero.lead: A built-in assistant that knows your VMs, apps, pools and networks. Ask why something is slow, what changed overnight or whether your photos are backed up. When you want it to act, it shows you a plan first and waits for your OK.

chat.title: Assistant
chat.question: Why is Jellyfin buffering tonight?
chat.offer: I can re-attach /dev/dri/renderD128 to the app and restart it. That takes about 20 seconds.
chat.answer: Jellyfin is transcoding 3 streams on the CPU. The shared iGPU isn't attached since this morning's update to 10.11.2, so hardware transcoding fell back to software. CPU on node-1 has been above 90% since 20:14.

does.heading: Questions, troubleshooting and actions in plain language.
does.lead: The assistant uses the same API as the console and the CLI. It sees what you can see and does what you can do, nothing more.

items.title: Ask about your setup
items.body: "Which VMs use the most RAM?" "What changed since yesterday?" It reads resources, metrics, logs, events, alerts and the audit log.

items.title: Troubleshoot
items.body: Links an alert to its likely cause, such as a full pool, a failing disk, an OOM kill or an expired certificate, and suggests a fix.

items.title: Take actions
items.body: Start or stop VMs, install an app from the catalog, snapshot a volume, add a firewall rule or run a backup. Every change is a plan you confirm.

items.title: Plan ahead
items.body: "Can this box take another Windows VM?" Capacity checks, config explanations and Compose imports drafted for you to review.

digest.title: Opt-in digest.
digest.body: A daily or weekly summary of alerts, updates and backup status, sent through your normal alert channels. It only reports; it never acts on its own.

models.heading: Local first. Nothing leaves your network unless you say so.
models.lead: The assistant stays off until you pick a provider. Setup suggests a local model sized to your hardware, and the chat always shows which model answered and whether data left the network.

items.title: Local, on the box
items.body: Ollama or llama.cpp from the catalog, running as an app with GPU passthrough if you have one.

items.title: Local, on your LAN
items.body: Point it at a model server on another machine, such as a desktop with a big GPU.

items.title: Remote, with your key
items.body: Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint or the Anthropic API. The key is stored as a platform secret.

grounded.heading: Every answer shows where it came from.
grounded.lead: It reads live state through the API, never a stale copy, plus the Crustates docs, ADRs and your own resource specs, indexed locally. Answers cite the resources, log lines and docs they used, with links straight into the console.
grounded.question: Is the photos share backed up?
grounded.answer: Yes. The last backup of tank/photos finished at 03:12 today: 1.8 GiB changed, 412 GiB total, verified. The next run is tonight at 03:00.

where.heading: In the console, the terminal and your own agents.

console.title: Web console
console.body: A chat drawer on every page that knows what you're looking at, so "restart this VM" just works.

cli.title: CLI
cli.body: Answers in your terminal, plans printed as diffs.

tui.title: Terminal UI
tui.body: An assistant pane in crust tui, next to your logs and resource lists.

mcp.title: Your agents, via MCP
mcp.body: Claude Code, Claude Desktop and other MCP clients use the same tools through the Crustates MCP server, with the same permissions.

safety.heading: Helpful, and on a short leash.
safety.lead: Models can be confidently wrong, so the assistant is built around review, not trust.

items.title: Acts as you
items.body: Your role and never more. A per-role allowlist decides which tools it may call at all.

items.title: Read-only by default
items.body: Every change is a plan: the diff, a dry run through the reconciler and its impact. Nothing applies without your confirmation.

items.title: Typed confirmation
items.body: Deletes, wipes, pool changes and risky firewall rules need you to type the resource name.

items.title: Audited and undoable
items.body: Actions are logged "via assistant" with the prompt behind them. Risky changes take a snapshot first.

items.title: Untrusted input stays data
items.body: Text in logs, app output, file names or web pages can never trigger an action. No autonomous actions.

items.title: Rate limits and budgets
items.body: Per-user limits and a token budget, so a looping model can't hammer the API or a paid provider.

destructive.heading: Type the name to delete it.
destructive.lead: The same guard the console uses. The assistant can propose it; only you can finish it.
destructive.body: Removes the VM and its 2 disks (96 GiB) on pool tank. A snapshot is kept for 7 days.
destructive.label: Type win11-old to confirm

items.title: Is it on by default?
items.body: No. It stays off until you pick a model provider in Settings.

items.title: What hardware do I need for a local model?
items.body: A small model runs on a modern CPU with 16 GB RAM. A GPU with 12 GB or more makes larger models responsive.

items.title: Does it send my data anywhere?
items.body: Only if you choose a remote provider. The chat shows a clear marker whenever data leaves your network.

items.title: When can I use it?
items.body: Questions and troubleshooting are planned for M4, actions with plan-and-confirm for M6. See the roadmap.

items.title: Can I turn off actions completely?
items.body: Yes. Admins can make it read-only for everyone or per role.

items.title: Can I use my own agent instead?
items.body: Yes. Connect Claude Code or any MCP client to the MCP server; the same rules apply.
